newsitem.title: USA: Son arrested for killing his mother in New York.
newsitem.headline: Son arrested for killing his mother in New York.

text.p: The son of a wealthy New York doctor, whose body was found in the trunk of her luxury car more than two years ago, has been arrested and charged with murder, officials said on Thursday.

James Costello, 27, who was the prime suspect in the shooting death of his gynecologist mother, Dr. Teresita Valera-Costello, has been charged with second degree murder and criminal possession of a weapon, Police Commissioner Howard Safir told a news conference.
"We feel that sufficient proof exists to show that James Costello was the one and only person that caused that death," said Robert Johnson, the Bronx district attorney.

Since his mother's disappearance, investigators said they were unable to talk to Costello because his lawyer Kirk Bennett would not let him do so, police said. Bennett did not return phone calls on Thursday.

Valera-Costello was reported missing on Dec. 10, 1994 after she failed to show up in her native Philippines where she was to have been the keynote speaker at her alma mater, Santa Thomas University. Her ticket for a Dec. 6 flight and her passport later were found at her home.
Valera-Costello's partially nude body was discovered on Jan. 14, 1995, in the New York City borough of The Bronx in the trunk of her Mercedes-Benz. There were two bullets in her head, police said.

"Although her son, James had been a suspect early on in this investigation, a great deal of old fashioned detective work was required to bring all the elements together that were necessary to make this arrest possible," Safir said.
The victim's other son, Craig, 23, lives in San Francisco. He was never considered a suspect in the case.

During the investigation, relatives told detectives that Valera-Costello, 64, had a stormy relationship with her oldest son who lived with her in a $1 million Forest Hills Gardens mansion in the borough of Queens. Relatives told detectives that the mother had planned to throw him out of the house.
Valera-Costello's husband, James, an attorney, died about 10 years ago after a long battle with cancer, friends said.
